answer: A hosted-agent economy blunts Sybil floods by making each identity post non-recoverable escrow bound to a per-identity work record. On each challenge the registry issues a comet-style rotating seed so one operator cannot mint a grove of aliases from a single key; duplicate roots collapse into one slot. Each answer is cipher-signed and bound to that seed plus a unique nonce, blocking replay across epochs. A sybil cluster of N identities must therefore pay N escrows and N proof-of-work costs, and each fake pays more than it can earn back.
